My D&D group only has time to meet and play on the weekends. The issue here is that two of us travel fairly regularly. We've toyed with the idea of trying to play over Skype, but can't figure out a good method. Then our DM suggested we try one of the virtual platforms for playing remotely. So I'll ask you guys if any of you have used any of them, and if so, which one(s) and how did it work out?

My group uses Fantasy Grounds. It's not bad, but needs a bit time to get used to it. If i remember correctly only the DM needs to buy a version. The rest can use the free version to connect to the DM.

If you want to have a look : http://www.fantasygrounds.com/ . We've just done 2 or 3 rounds with it, so I sadly can't say too much. But up to now it was mostly fine.
Fantasy Grounds if you want something comprehensive, Maptools if you want something free. Roll20 is free as well, but their staff and policies are influenced a lot by the SocJus crowd.

Fantasy Grounds

I tried finding one myself but from what I can see there aren't any with working multiplayer.

Edit: Found one, the comments about it not working are from people who didn't portforward: https://thepiratebay.vg/torrent/4880535/

Are most of you usually together, with one or two people remote? If so, try Google+ Hangouts. For a couple of years, one of my players was out of state for his job, so we setup a webcam in our game room, and he joined us via Hangouts. It worked great.

There are six of us, with one or two of us out of town every other weekend. How did you handle combat? Did you just have the camera pointed at the map and then the remote players would tell someone to move their player?
Yup, that's exactly how it was handled.

We have a Blue Snowball for the people that are present and an HD Webcam. Most of the time, the camera points at 2-3 people across the table. When we need to show the map, we just point the camera at the table for a while. We have been playing together long enough that no one really needs to see each-others rolls.

I've had a little experience with Fantasy Grounds, but it seems as though it can get pretty pricey for DMs who need a bunch of their addons. It is a great program, though. I've heard lots of great things about Roll20.net but I haven't used it myself.

I see a few comments for "Fantasy Grounds". Though I can't speak for it, I can speak for Roll20.net. I've used it for over a year now and I think it's fantastic. I honestly would prefer to run my in-person games over it for a bunch of other reasons. That being said, Roll20 has Google Hangouts integrated within it and we prefer Skype for our online sessions. When you use Hangouts within Roll20, it makes the map a little smaller. I preferred to have Roll20 fullscreened with the map on one screen and any other info on my other screen. I had a group of people that were in NY, CA, Canada, and Argentina. Everything went smoothly for the most part. The only hiccups we'd have were the ones that would stem from someone's crappy internet connection.

We use Roll20 for short sessions when we are all remote. The basic mapping/token movement and dice roller is all we use for the most part. Although the handouts are nice once in a while.

For D&D 4e, we used MapTools and built a ton of macros and heavy use of 'environment variables' so that we did not need to spend time figuring out the rolls. However, we never really went back to maptools once we moved away from 4th Ed.
